summary: Iteration 2 backend + frontend verified. Backend: 15/15 pytest tests passed covering anomaly-rules CRUD (5 defaults seeded with unique ids + system_default=true + enabled=true, create custom, toggle, PUT update, dry-run does not persist, DELETE decrements count, scan uses active rules and stamps rule_id/rule_name), Ops Agent chat (POST /api/chat returns {final, steps[], session_id}, at least metrics/list_anomalies tool called, session resume works, GET /api/chat/{sid} history persisted), Subject Lock insights (insight/alert/narrate modes all return non-empty insight + sweep_summary, GET lists >=3), camera frames timeline (ordered ascending by detected_at, count matches len(frames)), factsheet_with_locks with and without camera_id (subject_locks[] present, hits_in_window > 0 when class has ledger hits). Frontend smoke: nav-rules renders 5 default rule rows, new-rule-btn opens rule-editor modal, filling name+type=class_threshold+label=backpack+min_count=1+minutes=10 and clicking rule-save-btn adds it to the list; nav-assistant chat returns an assistant bubble within seconds; nav-cameras scrub-{id} opens track-scrubber-modal exposing scrub-slider + scrub-play and renders a frame image; nav-lock class/person Lock&Sweep works (12 sightings, 2 cameras), lock-insight-btn produces an insight rendered into lock-insights-list within a few seconds. Zero page errors, zero console errors during navigation. Note: iteration 1 features are untouched and still green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1281 lines (up from 928). Strongly recommend splitting into routers/ package (cameras, ledger, anomalies, rules, identities, locks, narrative, chat) before iteration 3 — the file is becoming hard to navigate.

PUT /api/anomaly-rules/{rid} uses `AnomalyRule` model and $set of `payload.model_dump()`. This wipes `system_default`, `created_at`, and `id` overlay flags. Not causing test failures but a partial-update (PATCH) style or preservation of managed fields would be safer. Currently the frontend re-sends most fields so it works.

In `_run_rule` for `class_threshold`, both `min_count` and `max_count` use OR logic and both set `hit=True` if either matches — for a rule that provides both bounds, the max_count check will always fire when count is between them but also if count is very high (only the min_count triggers), which is fine, but if only max_count is set it fires even when there are zero detections. Consider requiring explicit intent.

ops_agent.SYSTEM prompt still references `gpt-5.4` model name — iteration 1 confirmed this string works with the Emergent LLM key. If Emergent later revalidates keys, ensure model naming stays consistent between narrative and lock_insights endpoints (already consistent).

`sweep_lock` for kind='face' uses `identity_id` as the target — good. But there's no `plate` implementation despite ops_agent.tool_create_lock advertising `kind: face|class|plate` — plate sweeps will always return 0. Minor doc/impl mismatch.

`camera_frames` endpoint has no pagination cursor — `limit=200` is a hard cap. For long recording sessions the scrubber will silently truncate; consider adding an `offset` or `before/after` cursor when needed.
The `lock_insights` collection stores the full sweep_summary blob (including journey) per insight — over time this grows unboundedly. Consider TTL or capping to a reasonable rolling window.
seed_data_creation: Reused iteration 1 seed (2 demo cameras + TEST_video_cam with 6 processed frames). Tests created a TEST_ rule and TEST_ locks; the delete_rule test cleans up the rule and TestLockInsights.test_cleanup_lock closes its lock. A couple of extra active/closed locks remain from prior runs — non-blocking.
